exponents.title: What are Exponents?
exponents.intro: An exponent tells you how many times to multiply a number (the base) by itself.
exponents.meaning: Read as: 5 to the power of 3

zero.title: Zero Exponent Rule
zero.intro: Any number (except 0) raised to the power of 0 equals 1.

negative.title: Negative Exponents
negative.intro: A negative exponent means take the reciprocal (flip the fraction) and make the exponent positive.

scientific.title: Scientific Notation
scientific.intro: Scientific notation is a way to write very large or very small numbers using powers of 10.
scientific.condition: where 1 ≤ a < 10 and n is an integer

exponentVsPower.title: Exponents vs Powers: Understanding the Difference

laws.title: Laws of Exponents
laws.intro: These rules help us simplify expressions with exponents.

product.title: Product Rule
product.explanation: When multiplying powers with the same base, add the exponents.

quotient.title: Quotient Rule
quotient.explanation: When dividing powers with the same base, subtract the exponents.

power.title: Power of a Power Rule
power.explanation: When raising a power to another power, multiply the exponents.

productPower.title: Power of a Product Rule
productPower.explanation: When raising a product to a power, raise each factor to that power.

reading.title: How to Read Exponents
reading.caption: Different ways to say the same expression

exponentVsPower.title: Comparing Exponents and Powers
exponentVsPower.caption: Two related but different concepts
exponentVsPower.similarity1: Both terms are used in exponential notation
exponentVsPower.similarity2: Both describe the same mathematical expression
exponentVsPower.similarity3: The terms are often used interchangeably in everyday language
exponentVsPower.exponentDef: The small number written above and to the right of the base
exponentVsPower.powerDef: The result of the entire calculation (base raised to the exponent)
exponentVsPower.exponentUsage: "Raise to the exponent" or "the exponent of..."
exponentVsPower.powerUsage: "The power of..." or "raised to the power"
exponentVsPower.keyInsightText: The exponent tells you HOW MANY times to multiply, while the power is WHAT you get after multiplying.

zero.title: Zero Exponent Examples
zero.caption: Any non-zero number raised to 0 equals 1

scientific.title: Scientific Notation Examples
scientific.caption: Converting between standard form and scientific notation

example1.title: Using the Product Rule
example1.question: Simplify: 2³ × 2⁵
example1.step1: Identify: same base (2), so use product rule

example3.title: Power of a Power
example3.question: Simplify: (3²)³
example3.step1: Apply power of a power rule: multiply exponents

exercise2.question: What is 7⁰?
exercise2.hint: Remember: any non-zero number to the power of 0 equals 1.

notes.title: Tips & Tricks
notes.tip2: 📐 When in doubt, write out the multiplication: 2³ = 2 × 2 × 2
notes.tip3: 💡 Negative exponents flip to fractions, zero exponents always equal 1
notes.warning1: ⚠️ Don't confuse 2³ with 2 × 3! Exponents mean repeated multiplication, not regular multiplication.

conclusion.title: Outstanding Work! 🎉
conclusion.summary: You've mastered exponents and their laws! These powerful tools will be essential throughout algebra and beyond. Understanding exponents helps with scientific notation, polynomial operations, and many real-world applications.
conclusion.takeaway1: Exponents represent repeated multiplication of a base
conclusion.takeaway2: Product rule: add exponents when multiplying same bases
conclusion.takeaway3: Any non-zero number to the power of 0 equals 1
